A 2bp move pulls REFINANCERS off the fence and does NOTHING for purchase affordability — which is the cleanest statement of the rate-sensitivity split I have on this surface. Refi share rose to 41.9%, its highest in this run. ★★ THE YoY LEGS MOVED MATERIALLY AND ONE OF THEM MOVED IN MY FAVOUR AND ONE AGAINST — REPORT BOTH: refi improved from −22.2% YoY (wk 8/7) to −18% YoY, i.e. the base effect is unwinding, while PURCHASE went from −1.4% YoY to −3% YoY. ⇒ "NO REFI ESCAPE" STILL SURVIVES ON THE LEVEL BASIS (−18% YoY is a large deficit), BUT THE MARGIN OF SURVIVAL NARROWED BY 4.2pp IN ONE WEEK AND I AM RECORDING THAT RATHER THAN QUOTING THE OLDER, MORE FLATTERING NUMBER. If refi YoY keeps closing while purchase YoY keeps widening, the claim needs restating as a PURCHASE claim, not a refi one. ★ MBA own economist names affordability, not rates: Joel Kan — "affordability difficulties have reemerged as a reason for some homebuyers to delay purchase decisions." ★ AND THE SHARPEST DATUM IN THE RELEASE IS A LOAN SIZE, NOT AN INDEX: the AVERAGE REFINANCE LOAN SIZE FELL TO $282,200, THE LOWEST SINCE JUNE 2025 — MBA attributes it to larger-balance borrowers staying out. ⇒ THE REFI THAT IS HAPPENING IS SMALL-BALANCE. That is compositional evidence for the distressed-cohort claim from a direction I had not been measuring: it is not that refi volume is absent, it is that the refi that clears is at the small end. ⚠️ Do NOT read that as the 90+/thin-equity cohort refinancing — small balance is not the same as distressed, and MBA gives no credit or LTV split. It is a lead worth one pull, not a finding.
